El método lo desarrolló George Dantzig e: The method was developed by George Dantzig in 1947 for the United States Air Force: the problem was planning supplies and transport, with thousands of variables. His simplex algorithm walks the vertices intelligently instead of trying them all, and it is still the basis of logistics software across half the planet. Dantzig, as a student, arrived late to a class and copied from the blackboard two problems he took to be homework; he solved them in a few days. They were two open problems in statistics that nobody had been able to solve.
Que el óptimo esté siempre en un vértice: That the optimum is always at a vertex is what turns a problem with infinitely many possibilities into one with a short list to check, and that is what makes it genuinely solvable. With this idea airlines plan routes and loads, a refinery plans its blend of crudes, the cheapest diet meeting some nutritional requirements is found and a hospital's shifts are allocated. It is among the mathematics that moves most money in a day.
No siempre hay un único ganador. Convien: There is not always a single winner. It pays to recognise the three odd endings, because they come up in exams and because in practice they say useful things: that the problem is badly set up, that there are resources to spare, or that there are several equally good solutions and you can choose on some other ground.
